liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **I Just Want To Make Love To You** (2 reviews, 1 other source): The segue from this song into Women Are Smarter is praised; reviewer thinks it was the Muddy Waters tune's second and last performance; Reviewer calls this version among the funkiest the Dead ever played, apart from a few Shakedown Streets [1][17][19]
- **Loser** (2 reviews): Garcia plays exceptionally on Loser, especially at the vocal peak after the jam; Reviewer calls it the best Loser ever; Jerry's solo jam erupts powerfully, best played loud with good bass [20][28]
- **Keep Your Day Job** (1 review): Reviewer dislikes Day Job so much that they want to flee to the restroom when it starts [26]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Terrapin through Drums, Space and Morning Dew ran about 45 minutes, fitting on one side of a 90-minute cassette [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-07-22.108370.DaWeez.D5scott.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 154 min [1]
- **gd1984-07-22.sonyecm.unknown.gale.87037.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 158 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1984-07-22.150532.mtx.seamons.ht122.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 154 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [5]. Said about its sound: Low end is stronger than typical for an 80s recording; Phil is a bit hot in early songs [5]
- **gd84-07-22.sbd.bode.5959.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 153 min; rated 4.44/5 by 9 [6]. Said about its sound: PCM recording with no hiss; reviewer ranks it among the best-sounding 1984 tapes, alongside 11/2, 6/27 and 4/21; Midnight Hour and Brokedown come from a different soundboard, pitched about a half step slow with exaggerated treble [22][24]
- **gd1984-07-22.152323.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 154 min [7]
- **gd84-07-22.sbd.cole.5896.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 151 min; rated 4.4/5 by 15 [14]. Said about its sound: Bass levels are strong, which suits Phil fans; reviewer calls the soundboard stellar in sound [17]

## Around the show

- During Ship of Fools, a man cut his throat and wrists in a porta-potty; friends heard of it afterward [18]
- Compared with other 1984 tapes: 11/2, 6/27 and 4/21 (spaced Neumanns by Silberman) come close in sound quality [22]
- Reviewer saw Garcia barely open his eyes through the first set at Merriweather on 6/27/84, contrasting with this show's strength [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-07-22.108370.DaWeez.D5scott.flac16**: taped by DaWeez; transferred by D5scott; source: 2 Beyer M160 & 1 Sennheiser 421 Microphones > Nak MX100 W/2001 > Sony TC-D5M - analog master cassettes - TDK MA-R90's 30 feet from stage-center [1]
- **gd1984-07-22.sonyecm.unknown.gale.87037.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Dan Gale; source: Sony ECM-939LT (dead center, halfway between sbd and the stage) > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D6C) [3]. Also: Patches came from a soundboard via PCM and DAT, assembled in Samplitude, with crossfades and 48 to 44.1kHz resampling [3]
- **gd1984-07-22.150532.mtx.seamons.ht122.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack Pro > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) [5]. Also: Matrix of soundboard and audience sources; Da Weez's cassette contributed extra bass; dead air trimmed and clicks removed in Space [5]
- **gd84-07-22.sbd.bode.5959.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by DAT > CD> EAC> SHN (mkwACT) via Keith Bode; source: SBD> Cass Master> Dat [6]
- **gd1984-07-22.152323.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  April 2, 2021; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M) [7]. Also: A tape flip in Drums is covered by a PCM soundboard; tapes came from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton [7]
- **gd84-07-22.sbd.cole.5896.sbeok.shnf**: source: sbd> Cass Master> dats> wav> shn w/seek [14]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1984-07-22 Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1984-07-22-ticket/) [34]

A tape flip in Drums is covered by a PCM soundboard; tapes came from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton
